snippet.title: NEW SCAM ALERT: If You Answer, THEY STEAL EVERYTHING!
snippet.description:
Visit Our Sponsor ▶▶ For free and unbiased Medicare help, dial 609-633-4357 to speak with our trusted partner, Chapter -- or go to: https://askchapter.org/jeff
------------------------------------------
This video is a consumer protection warning about FBI and law-enforcement impostor scams that are targeting people across the country.

Scammers may pretend to be federal agents, local police, or government officials. They may threaten arrest, claim you are under investigation, or pressure you to send money, cash, gold, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or wire transfers. Real law enforcement agencies will not demand money over the phone, ask you to keep an investigation secret, or require immediate payment to avoid arrest.

In this report, we explain the red flags to watch for, how these impostor scams typically pressure victims, and the steps you can take to verify whether a call, message, or visit is legitimate. The goal of this video is to help viewers recognize the warning signs, avoid financial harm, and report suspicious activity safely.

If someone claiming to be from the FBI, police, Social Security, or another government agency contacts you and demands payment or secrecy, hang up or step away, then contact the agency directly using an official phone number you look up yourself, not one the caller gives you.

This video is presented for consumer education and public awareness. Its purpose is to help viewers recognize, avoid, and report fraud. It does not endorse or provide instructions for any illegal activity.

Plus: the new grocery shrinkflation list is here. 

We’re naming the brands shrinking packages, cutting portions, and charging you MORE for less food — often hoping you won’t notice. From snacks to frozen foods to household staples, we’ll show you the products getting smaller while prices keep climbing.
